claims.text: A graph neural network can predict melting temperature across the high-entropy-alloy family.
A graph neural network can predict the enthalpy of fusion of high-entropy alloys.
A graph neural network can predict the entropy of fusion of high-entropy alloys.
A graph neural network can predict volume change at melting for high-entropy alloys.
A graph neural network can predict liquid-phase thermodynamic properties of high-entropy alloys.
Machine-learning models learn patterns in existing data that enable prediction of thermodynamic properties.
Atomic structure and composition are the proposed information mediating the model's predictions.
The melting-temperature prediction will have a mean absolute error below 5% relative to experimental values.
The enthalpy-of-fusion prediction will have a mean absolute error below 3% relative to experimental values.
The entropy-of-fusion prediction will have a mean absolute error below 2% relative to experimental values.
The predicted volume change at melting will have a mean absolute error below 1% relative to experimental values.
Predicted liquid-phase thermodynamic properties will have a mean absolute error below 4% relative to experimental values.
The proposed applicability range is 500–2000 K and 1–10 atm.
The proposed model applies to high-entropy alloys containing 3–10 elements.
The proposed model applies to face-centered-cubic, body-centered-cubic, and hexagonal-close-packed atomic structures.
Model performance may depend on the quality and quantity of training data.
Model performance may depend on the complexity of alloy atomic structures and compositions.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis claims applicability across the high-entropy-alloy family, while the boundary restricts applicability to alloys with 3–10 elements and only FCC, BCC, or HCP structures.
